## K12 · K12-pump-once — process_ending pumps once per parked lend call; pumping once per endpoint changes R4b's notice order

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Architect · Revision: 3

Decision references: bad3803c6

Evidence: Ruled: batch. Notice order is not a rule; R3 now says so. Batching after all of a process's threads end also fixes a real departure: today a dying process's later thread can take a queued external call and end holding it (early Dead against R4b). Written in bad3803c6 (ipc.md R3 and residual, docs/todo/process-ending-pumps-once.md). Plan node K13 (needs K12).

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `5d18ab7d455f9eab3703b1ac50a6b7bf` · 2026-10-01T01:53:48Z

> K12 is review-ready (942234cd4). At the full fill it measures 23.6/20.5 ms (H/D) on rv32 and 23.3/20.5 on rv64, under the 25 budget. The 16-seed sweep passes 31 of 32; rv64 seed 16 is a test-fixture race in the steward's deadline loop, which K12 is fixing by setting the deadline after the spawn. Non-blocking question: process_ending is 8.0 ms, at its budget, and almost all of it is pump() run once per parked lend call (4 x ~1.2 ms). Pumping once per endpoint would cut ~3 ms but changes R4b's notice order. Is that order a rule (ipc.md R4b) worth keeping at this cost, or may the pump batch per endpoint, and if so, what does R4b say then? Not needed for K12's merge; it's margin for later, so rule when convenient and say if it's a follow-up page.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `f8780d38d8b89f18debbc1af715c2c84` · 2026-10-01T01:56:03Z

> Ruling: batch. Notice order is not a rule, so the pump may run once per endpoint, after all of the process's threads have ended. This is a follow-up, not K12's merge.
> 
> What the rules fix: R3 and I15 say each abandoned call gets one notice, to the thread holding it, on its endpoint, exactly once. "What receive returns" puts a thread's own abandoned notice before an exit notice, and that before messages. R4b says nothing about the order of notices. Among several notices owed to one thread, the code already gives the first by thread order and the rest by open-call index. That is now written in R3: one per receive, each exactly once, in no promised order.
> 
> Batching is also more correct than today. thread_ending pumps as each thread ends. A later thread of the same dying process that is still in Receive on that endpoint can then be picked. This needs a process that both calls and receives on one endpoint, which a hostile lease can arrange. That thread takes a queued external call and ends holding it, so the caller gets Dead. R4b says queued senders keep waiting for the restarted server. Nothing blocks it: process_ending and pump have no ending-process check, and find_thread sees every thread with an ipc frame. It is low severity, since there is no authority gain, only an early Dead. But the page states a rule the code doesn't keep.
> 
> Written in bad3803c6:
> - ipc.md R3: the order sentence.
> - ipc.md "Residual risks": a bullet linking the follow-up.
> - docs/todo/process-ending-pumps-once.md, listed in SUMMARY.md. Its "done when": first a case that shows the bug, then gather the served endpoints (at most MAX_THREADS, once each) and pump each once after all threads end. A lone thread's exit still pumps at once. Notices stay exactly once. Remeasure process_ending at the full fill.
> 
> Place it in a near-term kernel follow-up after K12. It's Tier A, size S. Decision refs for the resolve: bad3803c6.
